slides.say: A cyclist rides from home to work at a constant speed. If she rode twenty-five percent faster, the trip would take twelve minutes less. How many minutes does the trip take at her usual speed?
at: A cyclist rides from home to work

slides.say: So the route is the same, and the speed changes by a percent. They ask for the usual time, not the new one.
at: They ask for the usual time

slides.say: We'll solve it in two different ways. First by understanding, like in the lesson. Twenty-five percent faster is times five quarters. On the same route we flip it, so the time is times four fifths.
at: so the time is times four fifths

slides.say: The new time is four fifths of the usual time. So we save the remaining one fifth. The question says that saving is twelve minutes.
So one fifth of the usual time is twelve minutes. The usual time is five times twelve, sixty minutes.
Careful with forty-eight, choice number two. It's sixty minus twelve, the new time. And it's also what you get if you wrongly treat twelve as a quarter of the usual time. They ask for the usual time.
at: They ask for the usual time

slides.say: [pause] Now let's plug in the answers. We start again from the givens. Which choice do we try first? The choices are in order, thirty-six, forty-eight, sixty and seventy-two. So let's start with a middle one, forty-eight, choice number two. If it doesn't fit, it shows us which way to go.
So say the usual trip takes forty-eight minutes. Twenty-five percent faster on the same route means the time is times four fifths, like in the lesson. So she saves one fifth of the usual time.
at: she saves one fifth of the usual time

slides.say: A fifth of forty-eight is less than ten, because five times ten is fifty. But the question says she saves twelve minutes. So forty-eight saves too little.
at: A fifth of forty-eight is less than ten

slides.say: What does that tell us? The saving is always one fifth of the trip, so a longer trip saves more minutes. So the usual time must be bigger than forty-eight. Forty-eight is out, and thirty-six is out too.
at: a longer trip saves more minutes

slides.say: Forty-eight saved less than ten minutes, so thirty-six and forty-eight are out. Now let's try sixty minutes, choice number three, the next one up. A fifth of sixty is twelve, exactly the saving we need.
at: so thirty-six and forty-eight are out
so thirty-six and forty-eight are out
A fifth of sixty is twelve

slides.say: Let's also check sixty in the story itself. To make it easy, say the trip is sixty kilometers at sixty kilometers per hour. That takes one hour, sixty minutes.
Now she rides twenty-five percent faster. A quarter of sixty is fifteen, so sixty plus fifteen, seventy-five kilometers per hour.
Sixty kilometers at seventy-five is sixty over seventy-five, four fifths of an hour. That's forty-eight minutes.
Sixty minus forty-eight is twelve minutes less. That's exactly the given.
Choice number three is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
at: Choice number three is our answer
